chapters.name_meaning: The Yoga of the Despondency of Arjuna
chapters.summary: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Prince Arjuna experiences moral confusion and grief seeing his relatives and teachers arrayed for battle. He turns to Lord Krishna for guidance.

chapters.name_meaning: The Yoga of Knowledge and Reason
chapters.summary: Krishna begins His divine discourse, explaining the eternal nature of the soul, the path of selfless action, and the importance of equanimity.
Krishna explains the importance of performing one's duty without attachment to results, emphasizing karma yoga as a path to liberation.

chapters.name_meaning: The Yoga of Knowledge and Renunciation of Action
chapters.summary: Krishna reveals the history of yoga and His divine incarnations, explaining the distinction between action and inaction.

chapters.name_meaning: The Yoga of Renunciation of Action
chapters.summary: Krishna compares the paths of renunciation and action, explaining how both lead to liberation when done with the right understanding.

chapters.name_meaning: The Yoga of Self-Control and Meditation
chapters.summary: Krishna describes the practice of meditation, the qualities of a yogi, and the ultimate goal of self-realization.

chapters.name_en: The Yoga of Wisdom and Knowledge
chapters.name_meaning: The Yoga of Knowledge and Wisdom
chapters.summary: Krishna explains His divine nature, the difference between matter and spirit, and how devotees can know Him.

chapters.name_en: The Yoga of the Imperishable Absolute
chapters.name_meaning: The Yoga of the Eternal Divine
chapters.summary: Krishna describes the nature of the Supreme, the path to attaining Him, and the importance of remembering Him at the time of death.

chapters.name_en: The Yoga of Sovereign Knowledge and Sovereign Secret
chapters.name_meaning: The Yoga of Royal Knowledge and Royal Secret
chapters.summary: Krishna reveals the supreme secret of devotion and explains how all beings exist in Him and He pervades all creation.
Krishna describes His divine manifestations and opulences in the material world, revealing His infinite nature.

chapters.name_en: The Yoga of the Vision of the Universal Form
chapters.name_meaning: The Yoga of Beholding the Cosmic Form
chapters.summary: Arjuna requests to see Krishna's universal form. Krishna grants him divine vision and reveals His awe-inspiring cosmic form.
Krishna explains the path of devotion and describes the qualities of His true devotees.

chapters.name_en: The Yoga of Distinction Between Field and Knower of Field
chapters.name_meaning: The Yoga of Distinguishing the Field and the Knower
chapters.summary: Krishna explains the distinction between the body (field) and the soul (knower of the field), and the nature of knowledge.

chapters.name_en: The Yoga of the Three Qualities of Nature
chapters.name_meaning: The Yoga of Differentiation of Three Qualities
chapters.summary: Krishna describes the three modes of material nature (goodness, passion, ignorance) and how to transcend them.

chapters.name_en: The Yoga of the Supreme Person
chapters.name_meaning: The Yoga of the Supreme Divine Person
chapters.summary: Krishna describes the eternal tree of existence and reveals Himself as the Supreme Person beyond both the fallible and infallible.

chapters.name_en: The Yoga of Division Between Divine and Demoniacal
chapters.name_meaning: The Yoga of Distinguishing Divine and Demonic Natures
chapters.summary: Krishna describes the characteristics of divine and demoniac natures, and the importance of following the scriptures.

chapters.name_en: The Yoga of the Three Divisions of Faith
chapters.name_meaning: The Yoga of Three Types of Faith
chapters.summary: Krishna explains the three types of faith and how they influence one's practices, food preferences, and sacrifices.

chapters.name_en: The Yoga of Liberation Through Renunciation
chapters.name_meaning: The Yoga of Liberation Through Renunciation
chapters.summary: Krishna concludes His teachings, explaining true renunciation, the three types of knowledge and action, and offers the ultimate instruction.

verses.sloka_sanskrit: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच । धर्मक्षेत्रे कुरुक्षेत्रे समवेता युयुत्सवः । मामकाः पाण्डवाश्चैव किमकुर्वत सञ्जय ॥१॥
verses.transliteration: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca dharma-kṣetre kuru-kṣetre samavetā yuyutsavaḥ māmakāḥ pāṇḍavāś caiva kim akurvata sañjaya
verses.translation_en: Dhritarashtra said: O Sanjaya, after my sons and the sons of Pandu assembled in the place of pilgrimage at Kurukshetra, desiring to fight, what did they do?

verses.sloka_sanskrit: कर्मण्येवाधिकारस्ते मा फलेषु कदाचन । मा कर्मफलहेतुर्भूर्मा ते सङ्गोऽस्त्वकर्मणि ॥४७॥
verses.transliteration: karmaṇy-evādhikāras te mā phaleṣu kadācana mā karma-phala-hetur bhūr mā te saṅgo 'stv akarmaṇi
verses.translation_en: You have a right to perform your prescribed duty, but you are not entitled to the fruits of action. Never consider yourself the cause of the results of your activities, and never be attached to not doing your duty.
